paragraphs: Shemayah, a descendant of Sanheriv. He was nasi, Avtalyon's colleague; see his entry. Mishnah Hagigah, beginning of Ein Doreshin, and Eduyot 1:3, 5:6. Great sages, pupils of Shimon ben Shetah; see Akavyah ben Mahalalel. Hillel and Shammai received from them. They received in the year 3722 [תשכ״ב = 722; millennium inferred from context], 314 from the building of the Temple. Once a high priest came out of the Holy of Holies, and everyone followed him. When they saw Shemayah and Avtalyon, they left the high priest and followed them. When they came to take leave of the high priest, he said, “Let the sons of the nations go in peace.” They answered, “Let the sons of the nations who perform Aharon's deeds go in peace”: Yoma 71b. Keneset ha-Gedolah, Hoshen Mishpat, no. 7, asks how Shemayah and Avtalyon could have been court head and nasi, since the sages said that all appointments must be “from among your brothers,” and they were of converts. He answers that when they are accepted by the people it is permitted. But this is difficult: a nasi's law is like a king's, and it says, “From among your brothers”—the choicest of your brothers. One must say that a nasi's law is not like a king's; see עב״ש [unresolved bibliographic initials; E.B.Sh.] on Pesahim, Ahad Devarim. Perhaps their mother was an Israelite, so “from among your brothers” applies; see above, Avtalyon. So it appears explicitly in Derekh Hayyim, Avot, chapter 1: whoever explains that they themselves were converts is utterly mistaken, since one was nasi and the other court head, and all appointments must be from among your brothers. Rather, they descended from converts, and their mother was certainly an Israelite; see there, as Yuhasin writes about R' Akiva; see his entry. Yet it appears that they themselves were converts, not children of converts; see Avtalyon. Zekharyah's spirit was reincarnated in Shemayah; see Avtalyon. That high priest was Yoash's reincarnation; see Part I, year 3061. He is buried in Gush Halav; see Avtalyon.
